exposure: Gestational age at birth (39 weeks vs ≥42 weeks)
Post-term gestation beyond 41(+6) completed weeks of gestation
Mode of birth (vaginal vs instrumental vs emergency caesarean)
cohort: 95,631 women who gave birth at 39 completed weeks or ≥42 completed weeks in Australia
finding: Giving birth at ≥42 weeks gestation was associated with an increased risk of postpartum haemorrhage, shoulder dystocia, 3rd or 4th degree perineal tear, and unplanned caesarean section.
mod_finding: Giving birth at ≥42 weeks gestation was associated with an increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage following vaginal birth, instrumental birth, and emergency cesarean section.
